retired.fix_commit_subject: zle: port the SIGWINCH redraw, printfmt's % escapes + erase-to-EOL, M-t's NUL-terminator read, and insert_positions' second cline_str walk
retired.why: zle: … item 2 — printfmt's escape switch is now a line-by-line port of zle_tricky.c:2438-2535: %B/%b/%S/%s/%U/%u through tsetattrs/tunsetattrs, %F/%K through match_colour consuming the `{colour}` payload, %H through parsehighlight, %{ … %} terminated on `%}`, and an unknown escape emitting nothing instead of leaking its letter — which is exactly the `%Hhi%h` -> `Hhih` row this fixture recorded.
retired.evidence: re-verified first-hand by scripts/compsys_regressions.py under --variants: the fixture cell scored NOW-PASSES -> NOW-PASSES -> NOW-PASSES, and every variant and control of it came back NOW-PASSES. The runner reported the binary MOVED since the stamp (6420c23cecc13c35 -> 723088f811cdd366), which is the 'somebody fixed the bug' branch of the two the README names, not the 'the fixture was wrong' one.
retired.kept_because: a fixed bug is worth more as a guard than as a deleted file: the cell stays in the evidence base and the gate now FAILS if the divergence comes back.

guard_verified.against: /opt/homebrew/bin/zshrs -> Cellar/zshrs-all/0.12.49/bin/zshrs, the Homebrew-installed RELEASE build of the same version, 18273880 bytes, sha256 fb94500d8e1c32e7, built 2026-08-30 06:20:45 — before d555917f07 (08:04) and 44a3b4841c (08:32), so it still carries the bug
guard_verified.note: the flip is only worth something if the gate would CATCH the bug coming back, so it was pointed at a build that still has it: `compsys_regressions.py --zshrs /opt/homebrew/bin/zshrs --only explanation_percent_escapes`. It reported CONTROL-MOVED and exited 1. The harness detail it produced there is the same one observed_when_diverging records, so the guard fails on THIS bug and not merely on some difference.

observed.measured: 2026-08-30, commit 44a3b4841c, a byte-identical copy of target/debug/zshrs, passed with --zshrs (zshrs 0.12.49, 101620888 bytes, sha256 723088f811cdd366) vs zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0)
observed.notes: the whole listing agrees under BOTH strict modes the fixture always ran with — `--strict-stream` (the raw escape byte stream, not just the rendered grid) and `--compare-attrs` (SGR attributes, which is what rows 1/3/5 differed in). All eight -X groups agree, including the %F{red}, %H and %{X%} rows that carried the literal text.

observed_when_diverging.notes: One completer adds eight groups, each with a different escape in its -X explanation. %F{red} -> zshrs prints the literal '{red}'; %H -> zshrs prints 'Hhih'; %{X%} -> zshrs leaves a stray '%'. %B/%U/%S produce identical TEXT but zshrs emits no SGR at all (rows 1/3/5 differ in attributes only, so --compare-attrs is required to fail them). Only %% behaved identically. The trailing \e[K in the raw diff is fixture listing_row_erase_to_eol showing through.
observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: commit 3b4a01f0cd, target/debug/zshrs zshrs 0.12.49 (101601256 bytes, 2026-08-30 05:50:47), zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0) — this is the divergence AS MEASURED BEFORE 44a3b4841c. It is history, not current behaviour; the fixture now asserts the two shells AGREE.
